correctness.rationale: The binary hypergeometric law has only the two possibilities j-1,j with probabilities p,q; the corresponding binomial masses are equal exactly. The gamma/Stirling expansion is uniform away from endpoints. An endpoint factorial bound and a strict leading maximizer give global localization, then quartic degeneracy and the next quadratic Stirling term force O(sqrt(n)) imbalance and yield the limiting profile 4x^2/3-8x^4/3 with maxima at ±1/2 and height 1/6. Standard-library checker confirmed 357 rational/probability and high-precision finite identities; finite tests are not used to prove the infinite result.

originality.rationale: The 2024 motivating paper defines the count divergence and derives bounds, mostly for k<=n/2, but does not imply the leave-one-out optimizing composition or its square-root location and sharp 1/(6n^2) improvement. The 2020 hypergeometric-divergence bounds cover a related model but not the claim-level optimizer. Searches for the binomial modal-mass equivalent did not identify a covering theorem. Residual historical-priority uncertainty is recorded.
residual_risks: A generic historical theorem on optimizing binomial modal probabilities minus Bernoulli entropy may imply the same near-census asymptotic without sharing terminology.

value.rationale: Composition-dependent KL divergence is central to comparing replacement and without-replacement sampling. In the near-census regime, the leading balanced configuration is quartically degenerate, and the exact competition with the finite-population correction produces a nontrivial, sharp square-root shift and a universal second-order benefit. This is an infinite-family extremal characterization, not an unmotivated numerical slice.
